transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is good to see you again, Ms. Anderson. How have you been feeling since you got home?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am doing reasonably well, thank you. A bit tired, as expected, but the recovery is proceeding.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am really glad to hear you are feeling better. I can only imagine how draining the last week has been for you, especially trying to balance your recovery with everything you have going on.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It has been a challenge. I appreciate you saying that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to talk to you about your stay. While you were in the ward, there were some things that didn't go quite right regarding your post-operative care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean by that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was some confusion with the monitoring protocols. The team had a few issues with the timing of the checks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not following. Confusion about what? Specifically, what happened during my care?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a bit of a systemic breakdown in the workflow. We had some gaps in the observations.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Dr. Smith, I manage a hospital myself. I know how monitoring protocols work. Were your vital signs checked at the intervals prescribed in the surgical orders?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see this is frustrating for you. It must feel very unsettling to come back for a follow-up and feel like you are not getting a straight answer about your own health.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than unsettling. I am asking for a factual account. Did the team fail to monitor my blood pressure as ordered?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things just get so busy on the floor, and sometimes the communication between the nurses and the residents isn't seamless.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is an explanation for why it happens, not a description of what happened. Did my blood pressure drop?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a period where the numbers weren't where we wanted them to be, and it took a little while for that to be flagged.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long is a little while?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to check the rest of your chart for a moment, but generally, there was a delay in the frequency of the checks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a specific timeframe. If there was a failure in the standard of care, I need to know the exact duration of the undetected hypotension.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear how important this is to you, and I truly value your professionalism and your need for clarity. It is completely reasonable that you want the exact details.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then give them to me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't recall the exact minute on the spot, but there was an issue for a couple of hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A couple of hours? That is a significant window for a high-risk procedure. Who was responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The unit was very shorthanded that night, and the system for alerts didn't trigger as it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is anyone taking responsibility for this error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into how to prevent this from happening again. I really do care about your well-being and I want to make sure you feel supported today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the sentiment, but I am looking for an apology and a corrective action plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want us to move forward and focus on your healing now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot move forward without knowing the impact of those two hours of undetected low blood pressure on my kidney function and cardiac output.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are worried about the long-term effects, and that is a very valid fear to have after a surgery like this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not just worried, I am informed. This was a deviation from the prescribed care plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let me see if I can find someone to help me pull the exact logs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I would like that. I would also like a written incident report.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can see about that. Let's just wrap up the physical exam quickly so I can get you on your way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not finished with this conversation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand, but I have to go to another appointment in a few minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is unacceptable. You have admitted to a gap in care and now you are rushing out of the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do feel for the stress this is causing you. It is a very difficult conversation to have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It would be easier if you were transparent. What is the plan to ensure my current recovery isn't compromised by what happened in the hospital?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. Do I need additional blood work? Do I need a cardiology consult?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see how the next few weeks go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Dr. Smith, I am going to request a meeting with your Chief of Surgery and the Risk Management department.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I think we can just handle this internally.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am certain we cannot. I want a timeline for when I will receive the full records of the monitoring gaps.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll try to send an email when I can.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is too vague. I want a date and a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll check my schedule. I really have to get to my next patient now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap up the physical exam quickly', 'have to go to another appointment', 'have to get to my next patient now').

E.justification: Resident initially uses platitudes ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and only admits to a 'delay' after the patient repeatedly demands factual accounts.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the unit being 'shorthanded' and the 'system for alerts'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'unsettling', 'worried', 'valid fear') and references the patient's specific situation and professionalism.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague promises ('keep an eye on things', 'see how the next few weeks go', 'try to send an email when I can').
